title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC generative alone for propagation; false ends many
pass_a_gloss: Placeus grants the corruption is universal and hit other faculties, but for this debate only the generative mattered, because the issue was propagation of man, the path by which the corruption spreads. Concoction and nutrition are not lust-infected like generating; the generative tries to propagate other faculties as they are. After sin those faculties work less perfectly—hence disease and death from infancy—yet they remain subordinate ends for conserving the individual and propagating the species, not last ends. The true last end is only God; a false last end is one in genus but many in species and number—pleasure, utility, honor, and their many objects. So the many-last-ends scare does not force Placeus to make every vegetative work a rival summum bonum.
pass_b_english: PLAC. And that corruption is universal, and infected the other faculties too, but for the purpose only the generative one mattered, because the matter was the propagation of man, through which that corruption is propagated. But neither, as I already noted, are concoction and nutrition, like the act of generating, infected with lust, and the generative faculty tries to propagate the other faculties as they are. Meanwhile it is certain the concoctive and nutritive do not perform their functions as perfectly after sin was committed as before: and so all men from infancy are liable to various diseases and death; yet concoction and nutrition are not last ends, but only subordinate to the conservation of the individual and the propagation of the species. The true last end can be only one, namely God. But a false last end is one only in genus, and multiple in species and number; for either pleasure is sought, or utility, or honor, and of these also, for the various things in which they are sought, there is a great variety.
source_text: PLAC. Et universalis est illa corruptio, & alias etiam facultates infecit, sed ad propositum sola generans faciebat, quia de propagatione hominis, per quam propagatur illa corruptio, agebatur. Sed neque, ut jam monui, concoctio & nutritio sunt, ut actus generandi, infecti libidine, & facultas generandi caeteras facultates conatur quales sunt, propagare. Interim certum est non tam perfecte suas obire functiones concoctricem & altricem post peccatum admissum quam ante: itaque morbis variis & morti, etiam ab infantia omnes sunt obnoxii homines, nec tamen concoctio aut nutritio sunt ultimi fines, sed subordinati tantum conservationi individui & propagationi speciei. Finis ultimus verus non potest esse nisi unus, nimirum Deus. Sed finis ultimus falsus genere tantum unus est, specie autem & numero multiplex; vel enim voluptas quaeritur, vel utilitas, vel honor, horumque etiam pro variis rebus in quibus quaeruntur, magna est varietas.

choices.choice: Only generative for propagation debate; false last ends many in species
